digest.intro: A day with a few genuine sparks — Anthropic doing something quietly troubling, Stripe making a move that reshapes AI infrastructure, and some interesting material stuff at the edges of fabrication.

sections.heading: AI: the infrastructure and the ethics

items.title: Anthropic's watermark text adulteration in Claude is a perversion of writing
items.blurb: Gruber goes after Anthropic for invisibly altering Claude's output text to embed watermarks — not metadata, not a label, but manipulation of the writing itself. The framing matters: this is covert modification of language as a surface, and the implications for anyone using Claude as a writing tool are real.

items.title: Stripe will reportedly acquire OpenRouter for $7B+
items.blurb: OpenRouter — the clearinghouse that lets you route API calls across every major model — getting absorbed into Stripe turns AI access into a payments problem. That's a significant architectural bet: whoever owns the billing layer owns the abstraction layer.

items.title: The AI Credit Resale Economy
items.blurb: A look at the emerging shadow market of token brokers — entities buying AI credits in bulk and reselling them. Pairs directly with the OpenRouter acquisition story; this is what Stripe is actually buying into.

items.title: Laser Layers for (Almost) Isotropically Strong Prints
items.blurb: Using laser sintering between FDM layers to dramatically improve inter-layer adhesion — attacking the fundamental weakness of all extrusion printing. If this holds up, it changes what FDM parts are actually good for.

items.title: More On Wave Overhangs for 3D Printing
items.blurb: Wave overhangs extend arc overhang techniques to print near-horizontal geometry without supports. Slow going but the geometry is genuinely elegant — a print-path solution to a structural problem.

items.title: Desktop Colors — A museum for solid OS background colors
items.blurb: Someone built a quiet archive of the iconic solid-color desktops from classic operating systems. Unexpectedly moving — these colors were the ambient visual field of entire eras of computing.

items.title: Is This the World's Oldest Image of a Mind-Altering Plant?
items.blurb: A painted panel deep in a Spanish cave may push the human relationship with psychoactive plants back further than any previous evidence. The kind of find that makes you reconsider what the deep past was actually like.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film that operates as an essay on memory, ritual, and how cameras construct meaning — Marker wanders between Tokyo's vending machine shrines and Guinean funeral rites, treating footage as raw material for a theory of human consciousness. It will make you want to rebuild how you think about images entirely.

art_picks.title: Lee Bul — The Anatomy of Every Setting Sun
art_picks.creator: Lee Bul
art_picks.why: Lee Bul's work sits exactly at the edge you care about: cyborg bodies, utopian architecture collapsing into ruin, sci-fi mythology built from obsessive physical craft. Her suspended installation work in particular makes visible the invisible feedback loop between aspiration and entropy.

art_picks.title: Drexciya discography (starting with The Quest)
art_picks.creator: Drexciya
art_picks.why: A mythology built entirely in sound: James Stinson and Gerald Donald constructed an entire underwater civilization of the descendants of enslaved Africans thrown overboard during the Middle Passage, told through machine-perfect electro. It's world-building as resistance, identity, and systems design — with zero interviews or public appearances to explain it.

events.name: 2026 Whitney Biennial (closing weeks)
events.venue: Whitney Museum of American Art, 99 Gansevoort St, Manhattan
events.why: Last call on the 82nd Biennial, curated by Marcela Guerrero and Drew Sawyer — one of the three large NYC survey shows closing this month, and the one most likely to have contemporary artists working at the physical/digital and identity edge you respond to.

events.name: Lily van der Stokker — Male Art Exhibition, Great Show
events.why: Van der Stokker makes work that looks decorative and cheerful on the surface and is structurally corrosive underneath — her paintings interrogate gender, institutional power, and what counts as 'serious' art with a deadpan playfulness that earns it.

events.name: Acne Studios × Frédéric Malle Immersive Installation
events.venue: Éditions de Parfums Frédéric Malle, 120 Prince Street, SoHo
events.why: The Prince Street boutique has been transformed into an immersive Acne-pink bathroom environment — it's a case study in how two design-obsessed houses translate brand ethos into multisensory space, which is more interesting as an artifact of design thinking than as a shopping experience.

events.name: Dopplereffekt + DJ Stingray + bookworms
events.why: Dopplereffekt (Gerald Donald, the Drexciyan half who never plays live) alongside DJ Stingray in a raw Bushwick industrial space — machine music from one of electronic music's most hermetic mythologists, in the exact kind of environment where the social system is visible before it hardens.

events.name: Rival Consoles + Arushi Jain
events.venue: The Hall at Elsewhere, 599 Johnson Ave, Brooklyn
events.why: Rival Consoles makes meticulously structured electronic music where every patch and decay feels considered; Arushi Jain bridges North Indian classical vocals with modular synthesis — together it's a rare double bill where both acts are doing something genuinely their own.
